3	- **R-7vq.** A window’s size and client are its own: the pop-out can show a phone in the mobile app while the surface beside the chat fits the panel, and changing one never changes the other.
4	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/window @ popped-out*
5	- **R-c2m.** The page and the state on show belong to the design, so picking either moves every window showing it.
6	- **R-h9x.** Every design in a project offers the same sizes and clients: the ones its app shell declares, with Fit the panel always first.
7	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design @ typical*
8	- **R-e5n.** A custom size takes a width and a height between 200 and 4000 pixels; anything outside that shows the page fitting the panel.
9	- **R-w3j.** A design remembers one custom size, offered in every window’s size menu after the shell’s sizes; setting another replaces it.
10	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/window @ popped-out*
11	- **R-b6d.** A message may be images alone, with no words.
12	- **R-x8f.** The agent sees every image sent with a message, and the images stay with the session, so they’re still there when it’s opened again.
13	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/window @ popped-out*

I've built the change to Pop-out window. It turned out to be small: the design's `_window` didn't need porting, because it and every partial it includes (`_surface`, `_design-bar`, `_frame`, `_page-menu`) already match the app's views element for element. The only text difference was one line of a comment in `_design-bar`.

I haven't seen it render yet. Prelude's check runs after this turn and will say whether every state fits and how each page compares with its approved screen.

**What I changed:**
- **`server/main.js`, the window route's handler (`GET …/d/<design>/window`):** its model now includes `streaming`, which is what the agent is writing right now in the session the chat shows, or `null`. It's filled the same way as on the design page. The type already allowed `streaming` (`DesignPage` in `server/workspace.js`), so it didn't need changing. The window view doesn't display this text; it's there so the window's data matches the design's.
- **`prelude/design-workspace/routes.json`:** the window route's view is now `@app/server/views/_window`, and I removed its `"from"`.

Nothing else needed doing. The window's style (`:scope.window-page > .design`) is already in `server/public/workspace.css`, and RULES.md has no proposed rules, so I left it alone.

**Before you approve the screens:** since the markup didn't change, the window should match its approved screen in all eight states. If any of them differs, the cause is in the data or the styles, not the view, so check what the check reports there. The `building` state is the one that carries `streaming`.
